dedupe_keys.name: road criticality assessment for commuting under pluvial floods coupled flood and commute simulation

description: This study assesses the criticality of flooded road links for commuting by coupling pluvial flood modelling with a commute simulation under three scenarios (10, 30 and 50 year floods). Flood outputs are used to rebuild the road network, and the routes of each individual commuter are simulated for business as usual and each flood scenario. As the return period increased, traffic flow became more uneven; critical links were linked to proximity to water bodies, low-lying topography and high commuting demand, giving evidence to prioritise interventions for emergency response, risk management and urban planning. Coverage: one urban study area (not named in the abstract). Format and access: article in the Journal of Environmental Management (2023). Licence and cost: closed access. Caveats: data and code availability are not stated in the abstract records read. It supports network flow, agent-based and hazard exposure studies of urban roads under flooding. It relates to the Nordic Blue Spot road flood screening and the global rail and road climate exposure study in the catalogue.
